summary: A person holding a valid invite creates a vault client-side (salt, Master Key, Auth Key, DEK, encrypted profile record) before anything reaches the server, then submits it all in one transaction that also consumes the invite.

read.role: the only screen this feature drives
input and error-state conventions for the registration form, and the shell that delivers the default KDF envelope to this page

requestFields.value: invite token, username, Auth Key, salt, KDF parameter envelope, wrapped DEK + its nonce, profile record id, profile schema version, profile ciphertext, profile nonce — never the password

saltSize.value: 128 bits (16 bytes), crypto.getRandomValues, server rejects any other length with 400

dekSize.value: 256 bits, random, wrapped under the Master Key with AES-256-GCM

passwordPolicy.value: client-enforced only: >=12 characters and zxcvbn score >=3, no composition rules

usernameRule.value: normalized (trimmed, lowercased) before storage/comparison; allowed 3-32 chars, [a-z0-9._-]

mainCurrencySet.value: exactly the kind:currency rows of the operator's symbol table (rate-lookup.md), not full ISO 4217

profileRecordId.value: client-generated UUIDv4, profile AAD built with account_id empty, record_type: "profile", version: 1, entirely before the request is sent

initialProfilePayload.value: { mainCurrency, createdAt } only — the two required keys; idleLockMinutes and dimensions are absent until a later settings write

transactionScope.value: user row insert, profile record insert, and invite consumption all commit in one transaction, or none do

kdfEnvelopeSource.value: the server's current default KDF envelope, embedded on the GET /register page, used verbatim for derivation

kdfMinimumEnforcement.value: server rejects any submitted KDF parameters below its configured minimum with 400, even though the client UI never sends them

inviteErrorMessage.value: invalid, expired, used, and revoked invites all render the identical error page/message, no form

usernameEnumeration.value: accepted at this endpoint (invite-gated, small trusted audience) — a taken-username error is plain, not obfuscated; contrast login.md's decoy-salt defense

fixtures: a valid unused invite (from admin-invites.md) for the happy path, plus one each of invalid/expired/used/revoked for the byte-identical-error assertion
a captured request payload from a real registration, to assert absence of password/Master Key/unwrapped DEK
a known AAD fixture for the profile blob (account_id empty, record_type profile, version 1), built client-side with no server interaction
a KDF-parameters-below-minimum payload and a non-16-byte salt payload, for the two server-side rejection criteria
focus: the request-body-contains-no-secret assertion must inspect the actual serialized payload, not just trust the client code path
the 'registration is one transaction' criterion needs a simulated failure between the user insert and the profile insert to prove no partial state — a happy-path test alone doesn't show this
byte-identical invite error responses is a shared assertion with admin-invites.md; verify it's asserted once against real HTTP responses across all four invite states, not paraphrased per state

the profile record indistinguishability criterion ('same validation, same column values, same AAD' as an ordinary PUT /api/records) needs a direct comparison against a record-api.md-path write, not just 'it looks like a profile record'
